title: Review a component with unnecessary global state
description: Problem: Review a component with unnecessary global state. Solve this problem with multiple approaches and detailed explanations.

data.text: **Review a component with unnecessary global state** is a state-management smell. When a component lifts local UI state into Redux, Context, or a global store without a real need, it couples unrelated features, makes testing harder, and creates unnecessary re-renders. The question in a senior review is not whether global state is bad, but whether this particular piece of state needs to be global at all.

data.title: What to look for
items: A modal open flag stored in Redux when only the parent component uses it
Form input values synced to a global store on every keystroke
A theme toggle or sidebar collapse state living in Context when it is used by one route
Selected row ID in a table lifted to global state instead of local component state
Cached API responses stored in global state instead of a dedicated data-fetching cache
Derived data stored as separate global state instead of being computed during render

terms.definition: Moving state to the nearest common ancestor so siblings can share it, without making it global.
Keeping state as close as possible to where it is used, reducing the blast radius of updates.
Passing props through intermediate components that do not use them. Often a sign that state should be colocated or a context split.
State stored outside the component tree, accessible from anywhere. Examples: Redux, Zustand, Jotai, React Context.
The number of components that must re-render when a piece of state changes. Global state typically has a large blast radius.

data.text: Before approving a global state decision, ask three questions. First, does more than one sibling or branch need this value? If not, lift it to the nearest shared parent. Second, does the value need to persist across navigation or page refreshes? If not, local state or a URL parameter is simpler. Third, is the value derived from other state? If so, compute it during render instead of storing it.

data.title: Unnecessary global state
data.content: A modal open flag is stored in Redux even though only the SettingsPage needs it. Every reducer subscription re-renders SettingsPage when unrelated actions dispatch:

data.title: Local state instead
data.content: Moving the flag to local component state removes the global coupling and eliminates unnecessary re-renders from other reducers:

items: The value is needed by deeply nested components that share no closer ancestor
The value must survive navigation and survive across page refreshes via persistence
Multiple features need to read and write the same value concurrently
The value drives URL or meta tags and must be kept in sync with routing
The value is expensive to compute and caching it globally benefits many consumers

cards.title: Local state
cards.description: useState or useReducer inside the component that owns the data.
cons: Cannot share across branches without lifting

cards.title: Lifted state
cards.description: State lives in the nearest common parent and flows down via props.
cons: Parent must re-render on every change

cards.title: Context
cards.description: React Context broadcasts a value to any consumer in the subtree.
cons: All consumers re-render on value change
Can be misused as global state

cards.title: Global store
cards.description: Redux, Zustand, Jotai, or similar stores with selectors and subscriptions.

data.title: Prefer local state
data.text: The best global-state decision is the one you do not make. Start with local state. If prop drilling becomes painful, extract a small context for that feature only. Only reach for a global store when the data genuinely belongs to many unrelated parts of the app.

items.text: List every piece of state in the global store and its consumers
items.hint: Search the codebase for the action type or state path

items.text: For each item, ask whether more than one sibling needs it
items.hint: If only one route uses it, move it to local state

items.text: Check whether derived values are stored instead of computed
items.hint: Use selectors or derived variables instead of duplicating state

items.text: Verify the component still passes tests after moving state
items.hint: Local state is easier to mock and assert than global store state

data.title: Audit and refactor global state
data.description: Pick a component in your current project that reads from Redux or Context. Audit whether that state is truly global or could live locally. Refactor it to the narrowest possible location and verify tests still pass.
steps: Identify a component with global state that feels heavy
List all consumers of that state across the codebase
Move the state to the nearest shared parent or convert to local state
Run the test suite and fix any broken snapshots or mocks
Measure render count with React DevTools Profiler to confirm the blast radius shrank
data.expectedOutcome: You should see fewer re-renders in the profiler and simpler component tests after moving state closer to its consumers.

items.question: Is Context the same as global state?
items.answer: Context is a transport mechanism, not a state manager. You can use Context to provide a small, feature-scoped store without making it global. The problem arises when Context is used as a catch-all for everything.

items.question: How do I know if prop drilling is real or imagined?
items.answer: Prop drilling becomes a problem when intermediate components receive props only to pass them down, and changing the prop type requires touching many files. That is the signal to extract a context or split the component tree.

items.question: Should every form use local state?
items.answer: Yes, unless the form value is needed by another route or must survive unmount. For most forms, local state or uncontrolled inputs are simpler and faster than syncing to a global store on every keystroke.

data.title: Summary
points: Start with local state and lift only when siblings need to share data
Use Context for feature-scoped state, not as a global store
Measure re-render blast radius before and after moving state
Avoid storing derived values or transient UI flags globally
Refactor global state when it couples unrelated features
data.takeaway: A senior review judges global state by whether it is earned, not by whether it exists. The simplest state location is almost always the best.
